page: Amazon Web Services c9g.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the custom 64-bit Arm-based AWS Graviton family featuring Neoverse-V3 cores. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, it provides 4 dedicated physical CPU cores and 4 vCPUs running at a clock frequency of 3.3 GHz with a single thread per core. The processor architecture includes 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache, paired with 8.0 GB of RAM at a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Local NVMe disk storage is not included, and baseline network throughput is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark analysis shows exceptional single-thread performance alongside balanced multi-threaded execution. The instance ranks in the top 10 percent for single-core Geekbench execution, single-threaded compression and decompression, text processing, and memory bandwidth tests. Multi-core CPU benchmarks, software compilation, static web serving, and database operations rank within average benchmark tiers. PassMark CPU aggregate scores and specialized hardware encryption tests show lower relative positioning, while medium LLM prompt processing shows lower efficiency due to core and memory boundaries.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides efficient hardware density for compute-bound tasks that do not demand extensive RAM capacity per vCPU. Because local storage is absent, storage needs must be met via attached cloud block volumes. This instance configuration is well suited for microservices, web application backends, code compilation pipelines, text analytics, and general-purpose compute processing.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier performance in single-core Geekbench tasks, text processing, and memory bandwidth tests. Multi-core operations, static web serving, and database transactions perform within average ranges, whereas hardware encryption and PassMark aggregate CPU scores rank in lower tiers. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides high compute density per gigabyte, making c9g.xlarge suitable for single-thread bound workloads, microservices, build nodes, and general compute jobs that do not require ephemeral local storage or large memory allocations.
